test_policy.notes: "ACT/SAT scores are not required as part of the admission process. You may choose to submit ACT/SAT scores if you wish." SLU does not accept superscores: send the composite and all subscores from each completed test. Nursing prefers a score (a submitted score must be at least 24 ACT / 1160 SAT to be considered). International students still have to show English proficiency, which can be met with an SAT/ACT score (see English).

requirements.notes: No application fee for undergraduate admission, through the SLU application, the Common Application or the Coalition application (Scoir). Required: high school transcript(s) sent electronically to admission@slu.edu (international: academic records in English translation for every secondary and post-secondary school attended; official final transcript and any school-leaving exam results before enrollment) and proof of English proficiency unless waived. Test scores, the Secondary School Report (counselor form), a resume and letters of recommendation are listed as "Though not required for admission" but strongly encouraged; an admission interview is encouraged (arranged with the admission counselor; the page does not say whether it is evaluated, so interview is left null). The international page says the application asks first-time freshmen for an essay; the first-year pages do not list an essay requirement, so supplemental_essays is left null. Proof of financial support is needed for the I-20 (SLU's FAQ estimates $70,000 for one undergraduate year) but "does not impact your admission decision". Nursing, occupational therapy, physical therapy and flight science have a Dec. 1 application deadline (supporting documents due Dec. 11 for nursing, OT and PT, which also need a 3.20 minimum GPA). Regular decision is accepted on a space-available basis.

deadlines.label: Early Decision I
deadlines.notes: Binding; the Early Decision Agreement must be signed by all parties. Notification begins Dec. 1. The page lists one set of dates for all first-year applicants (no separate international deadline) and shows no year; it says 'Apply to Summer or Fall 2027', so Nov. 2, 2026 is read for fall 2027 entry. If incomplete on Dec. 1 the applicant must switch pathway.

deadlines.label: Early Action
deadlines.notes: Non-binding. Notification by Feb. 1. Dec. 1 is also the Scholars Programs application deadline. The page shows no year (fall 2027 entry assumed from 'Apply to Summer or Fall 2027').

deadlines.label: Early Decision II
deadlines.notes: Binding. Notification begins Feb. 1. Incomplete applications on Feb. 1 move to Regular Decision. The page shows no year (fall 2027 entry assumed).

deadlines.label: Regular Decision (preferred by April 1)
deadlines.note: By April 15 for completed applications by March 16
deadlines.notes: "Preferred by April 1; SLU will continue accepting applications and awarding scholarships while space is available." Decisions by April 15 for completed applications by March 16, otherwise within 30 days of a complete file. Nursing, occupational therapy, physical therapy and flight science: Dec. 1.

deadlines.label: Merit scholarships: apply by Dec. 1 for automatic consideration
deadlines.notes: No separate application; later applicants are considered as funds allow. Separate applications (Presidential and Martin Luther King Jr. scholarships; honors and scholars programs) open Sept. 1 in the Billiken Gateway portal; the MLK application with its resume and essay is due Feb. 1. The page shows no year (fall 2027 entry assumed).

english_policy.waiver_notes: International applicants must show English proficiency unless waived: (1) citizens of the English-speaking countries on SLU's list (e.g. Australia, Canada except Quebec, Ireland, New Zealand, Nigeria, South Africa, UK, US); (2) the entire high school curriculum in English, with official documentation from the school; (3) a college-level (non-ESL) English course at an accredited US college. Also accepted at the minimums on the page: SAT evidence-based reading and writing 550, ACT English 21, AP Language or Literature 4, IB English A Language and Literature HL 6, TOEFL Essentials 8.5, TOEFL ITP Plus for China 627, TOEFL PBT 550, Gaokao (middle of Tier 2 or better and English 125/150, interview required). Scores must be sent directly by the testing agency (TOEFL/SAT code 6629, ACT 2352) and are valid two years; allow about 4 weeks. All new students take an English writing placement exam and many take the SLU Writing Exam (SLUWE); applicants below direct-entry minimums can use INTO SLU English programs.

english.notes: Minimum for admission; graduate programs may be higher. The page lists no TOEFL iBT subscore minimums and no separate minimum for the new 1-6 scale.
Minimum score for admission (Pearson Test of English).

aid.notes: SLU's FAQ says "Financial aid is available to international students attending the St. Louis campus" but describes only merit aid: international applicants are "automatically considered for SLU's merit-based scholarships" with the application (no separate form); apply by Dec. 1 for full consideration. First-year merit awards are up to $15,500 (Billiken), $16,500 (Ignatian), $17,500 (University) or $19,500 (Vice Presidents') per semester for up to 10 semesters, based on prior academic performance. The Presidential and Martin Luther King Jr. scholarships need separate applications. The need-based SLU Tuition Promise requires the FAFSA and federal aid eligibility, so international students do not qualify; no international need-based aid page and no CSS Profile requirement were found.

majors.program: Nursing BSN (Trudy Busch Valentine School of Nursing)
majors.notes: Dec. 1 application deadline; minimum high school GPA 3.20 on a 4.00 scale with emphasis on math and science; test optional but preferred (a submitted score must be at least 24 ACT / 1160 SAT; students accepted in previous years averaged 28 ACT / 1310 SAT). Strong applicants have four years of math and of science.

sat.note: SLU's ETS code for TOEFL and SAT scores is 6629.

pte.note: No institution code is listed; send the PTE score report to Saint Louis University.

tier_notes.general: Judgment call, no published ranking used: private Catholic (Jesuit) doctoral university in a large city, 75% admit rate (IPEDS fall 2024), SAT section medians 650 reading/writing and 655 math; placed with Pepperdine and Oregon (C), below Fordham (C++).
tier_notes.pre_med: B: a medical school on campus and a separate Medical Scholars Program (listed on the admission pages) make health-professions advising unusually strong for a C general-tier school. Judgment, not a ranking.
